messages.subject: model algebra especification
parts:
Dear all, I am working with an N-mixture model with random effects and want to check if I am writing the algebra correctly. I have several bird counts (samples) in each ranch (or farm), so farm identity is the random intercept (beta0,R). Is this the correct sequence of equations?  I also want to explain how the Poisson and Binomial processes connect to estimate Ni but can´t figure out how the model works. I appreciate comments in this regard too. 

Thanks so much. Joaquín.  



--
Joaquín Aldabe

Departamento de Sistemas Agrarios y Paisajes Culturales
Centro Universitario de la Región Este, Universidad de la República, Uruguay
Ruta 15 (y Ruta 9), Km 28.500, Departamento de Rocha  
                                                          https://sites.google.com/site/perfilprofesionaljoaquinaldabe/home

messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] model algebra especification
parts:
Dear Joaquin,

 

mostly correct, but:

  • i in the first line should be a subscript
  • Also in the first line, you need a subscript i for lambda
  • Line 2: make a twiddle instead of the equal sign
  • Line 3: you want the I to be a subscript for lambda and then I think you need a plus sign in the latter parts of that line
  • Line 4: make this a twiddle instead of an equal sign

 

Otherwise, it looks good to me.

 

Best regards --- Marc

In year 1, all ranches had the same management, while in year 2, 6 ranches had changed their management. That´s why I´m interested in assessing the interaction term..

Hope this helps to figure out the algebra. 

Thanks so much!

Joaquín.

parts: The variable Temporada corresponds to the year (1 or 2), Manejo is management and Potrero means field id. Sorry for sending in spanish.

El jue, 4 ago 2022 a las 15:52, <joaquin...@gmail.com> escribió:

Hi Marc, the unit in the experiment is the field, that is nested in ranch (i.e. several fields were sampled in each ranch). I put Year as a variable (column) with two levels (year 1 and year 2). I want to know if year has a effect on field abundance at control and treatment ranches. I attached the dataset. Let me know if you need further explanation or information.

 

Thanks so much for your time!

 

De: unma...@googlegroups.com <unma...@googlegroups.com> En nombre de Marc Kery
Enviado el: jueves, 4 de agosto de 2022 15:47
Para: unmarked <unma...@googlegroups.com>

Dear Joaquin,

 

OK, thanks. Question back:

  • so what's the unit in the experiment ? The field/paddock ?
  • And how did you organize the data for the two years ? Stack them on top of each other ?

Thanks and best regards  -- Marc

 

 

 

From: unma...@googlegroups.com <unma...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of joaquin...@gmail.com <joaquin...@gmail.com>
Sent: Thursday, August 4, 2022 18:39
To: unmarked <unma...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Re: [unmarked] model algebra especification

 

Hi Marc, I used ubms package. So I don´t have BUGS code. My data consists on 11 ranches. In each ranch I sampled several fields or paddocks. I did this in two different years. In year 1, all ranches had the same management, while in year 2, 6 ranches had changed their management. So, I have 5 ranches as control (no changes in management) and 6 ranches that changed management (treatment). So I´m assessing if year affected treated ranches but not control ranches. That´s why I´m interested in assessing the interaction term..

 

Hope this helps to figure out the algebra. 

 

Thanks so much!

 

Joaquín. 

 

El jueves, 4 de agosto de 2022 a las 10:55:15 UTC-3, Kery Marc escribió:

Dear Joaquin,

 

If you send me the BUGS language code offline I can make an attempt. I realize now that you may also need some index t for year perhaps.

 

Thanks and best regards  -- Marc

 

 

 

Von: unma...@googlegroups.com <unma...@googlegroups.com> Im Auftrag von joaquin...@gmail.com
Gesendet: Donnerstag, 4. August 2022 15:51
An: unmarked <unma...@googlegroups.com>
Betreff: Re: [unmarked] model algebra especification

 

Thanks Marc! in line 4 I want to express a interaction between Year and Management. That´s why I used a X. Do you knwo how to algebraically express that?

 

Best,

Joaquín

El jueves, 4 de agosto de 2022 a las 5:02:23 UTC-3, Kery Marc escribió:

Dear Joaquin,

 

mostly correct, but:

  • i in the first line should be a subscript
  • Also in the first line, you need a subscript i for lambda
  • Line 2: make a twiddle instead of the equal sign
  • Line 3: you want the I to be a subscript for lambda and then I think you need a plus sign in the latter parts of that line
  • Line 4: make this a twiddle instead of an equal sign

 

Otherwise, it looks good to me.

 

Best regards --- Marc

 

Von: unma...@googlegroups.com <unma...@googlegroups.com> Im Auftrag von Joaquín Aldabe
Gesendet: Mittwoch, 3. August 2022 21:11
An: unma...@googlegroups.com
Betreff: [unmarked] model algebra especification

 

Dear all, I am working with an N-mixture model with random effects and want to check if I am writing the algebra correctly. I have several bird counts (samples) in each ranch (or farm), so farm identity is the random intercept (beta0,R). Is this the correct sequence of equations?  I also want to explain how the Poisson and Binomial processes connect to estimate Ni but can´t figure out how the model works. I appreciate comments in this regard too. 

 

Thanks so much. Joaquín.
